item.title: Parsing Ambiguous Time Zone Abbreviations in .NET DateTime
item.description:
“Parsing Ambiguous Time Zone Abbreviations in .NET DateTime”

When dealing with date and time strings that include three or four-letter time zone abbreviations (like “CEST”, “CST”, or “AMT”), developers using C# and the .NET framework often encounter parsing failures or, worse, incorrect time conversions due to ambiguity. How can one reliably convert these strings into usable DateTime objects?

The core issue stems from the fact that these short abbreviations do not map uniquely to a specific time zone offset; they are context-dependent based on culture or geography. For instance, “AMT” can mean “Armenia Time” (UTC +4) or “Amazon Time” (UTC -4).
